sections.advice: Queenstown → Crown Terrace is 16 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.
Crown Terrace → Crown Range Summit climbs about 1121 m in 10 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.
Crown Range Summit → Cardrona drops about 1121 m over 16 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.
Cardrona → Wanaka is 31 km of rhythm rather than effort. Let it flow and let the view breathe.

crown-range-road.provenance: CURATED FROM THE ARCHIVE: waypoints taken from the named road Crown Range Road. Distances between stops are great-circle with a road factor, not a routed measurement - the pipeline replaces them when it routes this line.

scenicChapters.title: Crown Range Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 10.9%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter — first and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Crown Range Road
scenicChapters.narrative: 1121 m come off over 15 km at around 7.2%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it. Brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

crown-range-road.story: Out of Queenstown, one way: 70 km, roughly 1 h 09 in the saddle. On the way it passes Crown Terrace, Crown Range Summit and Cardrona. The highest point is about 1,100 m. A steady touring day rather than a sprint.
